title: Erdős–Ko–Rado: k-uniform intersecting families (formalize-only)
why_not_classical: Erdős–Ko–Rado 1961 (announced; proof dating to 1938) is a completely settled landmark of extremal set theory: if n ≥ 2k, every intersecting family of k-subsets of an n-set has size at most C(n-1, k-1), achieved by a star. This is NOT an open problem. Value is a Mathlib contribution (k-uniform intersecting bound), not a discovery. Do NOT re-fund as novel. Uniqueness of stars for n > 2k is classical too — optional stretch, not required for v1.
recommendation: RECOMMENDED PRIME — genuinely NEW proof layer over upstream SetFamily infra. Mathlib v4.10.0 already has the NON-UNIFORM intersecting bound (Set.Intersecting.card_le: |F| ≤ 2^{n-1} on a boolean lattice) plus Shadow, LYM, Sperner, Kleitman. It does NOT have the k-uniform EKR bound. Katona's cycle method is a finite double-count (cyclic permutations × interval k-sets) that maps cleanly to Finset/Nat.choose; n=2k complementary pairing is a one-heartbeat partial. Eligibility: not a re-warm of Sperner (antichains vs intersecting k-sets) nor of Intersecting.card_le (wrong uniformity).

statement_pin_required.convention: Fix n k : ℕ with 2 * k ≤ n. Let F be a Finset of k-element Finsets of Fin n. Intersecting means ∀ A B ∈ F, A ∩ B ≠ ∅. Claim: F.card ≤ (n-1).choose (k-1). Star construction: for any i : Fin n, {A | i ∈ A} is intersecting of that size.
landmines: n ≥ 2k is ESSENTIAL. If n < 2k every two k-sets intersect and the max is C(n,k), not C(n-1,k-1). Do not state the bound without the hypothesis.
Do NOT cite Mathlib Intersecting.card_le as EKR — that is the non-uniform boolean-lattice half-power-set bound.
k = 0 / k > n edge cases: pin k ≥ 1 and k ≤ n (or prove trivially separately).
Equality uniqueness (stars unique for n > 2k; complementary pairs when n = 2k) is OUT OF v1 scope unless leftover budget.
statement_pin_required.canonical_source: P. Erdős, C. Ko, R. Rado, Intersection theorems for systems of finite sets, Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) 12 (1961) 313–320. Proof pin: Katona cycle method (cyclic permutations; interval k-sets).

feasibility_shape: Level A: definitions + star construction meets the bound + n=2k complementary pairing. Level B: Katona cycle double-count for n ≥ 2k. No SAT/native_decide explosion; no offline witness search.
